role_and_message.evidence: The motivation remains comparison of annotation requirements, annotation costs and annotation speed for five oriented-detection paradigms.

panel_and_object_coverage.evidence: All original (a)-(e) panels remain, including both horizontal-box and point-label 20% branches within partial weak supervision and their 80% unlabeled data.

labels_math_and_numbers.evidence: All original cost values $86/1k, $63/1k, $42/1k and times 0.2, the 20%/80% labels, method names and PWOOD identity are retained in the restored panels.

connections_and_direction.evidence: Panels are reordered into full weak/strong annotation types above and partial-label settings below. Added headings correctly associate rotated boxes with semi-supervision and horizontal boxes or points with partial weak supervision.

visual_encodings.evidence: Original red high-cost, blue middle-cost and green low-cost wording and all annotated green boxes/points are unchanged. New framing does not redefine them.

examples_and_data.evidence: All aerial photographs, annotated rotated/horizontal boxes, points, unlabeled image stacks, original prices and method lists are preserved in complete original scientific panels.

unsupported_additions.evidence: The new annotation-cost/speed clarification and 20%-labeled-plus-80%-unlabeled summary are directly visible in the source and supported by the caption and first-page introduction.

complete_visible_content.evidence: Both alternatives in partial weak supervision are fully visible; no lost point branch, clipped price, missing method list or obscured annotation remains.

remaining_limitations: Original examples, content and source resolution remain; new text is limited to original caption/body claims. Layout quality is assessed separately.
caption:
Fig. 1. The main paradigmatic types of existing oriented object detec-
tion. Existing methods are primarily divided into rotated boxes (RBox)-
supervised, horizontal boxes (HBox)-supervised, Point-supervised, and Semi-
Supervised approaches. Compared to these settings, our proposed Partial
Weakly-supervised methods have high annotation speed and low costs.
